title: Generic containment of fibre associated points spreads to a nonempty base open
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], and let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume that $|Y|$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] and let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. For $y\in Y$, use the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ and the tensor pullback $F_y$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; associated points are [def-trf-relative-assassin]. If $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_\eta}(F_\eta)\subseteq |U_\eta|$, there exists a nonempty open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in |V|$ one has $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(F_y)\subseteq |U_y|$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $U$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generic-flat-reduced-base-model] to $f$: it gives an integral affine open $W$ of $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$, mapping homeomorphically onto a nonempty open $V_0\subseteq Y$, with identical residue fields and identical scheme fibres. Set $X_W=X\times_YW$, $F_W=q_X^*F$ and $U_W=q_X^{-1}U$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]; and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type] ensures that $F_W$ is of finite type, with the same local generating bounds. The generic containment hypothesis transfers to $W$ by [lem-sfb-fibre-assassin-containment-base-change], applied to $W\to Y$. A nonempty open of $W$ with the required containment therefore gives an open of $Y$ with the same property, by the reverse implication of the same node at every point. It suffices henceforth to prove the result over $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a domain and generic field $K$. The extra flatness of $X_W\to W$ supplied by the reduction tool is not needed.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), first paragraph, reduction and affine base restriction; the existing generic-flat reduced-base tool packages these operations.

proof.text: By the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose a finite affine covering $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^rX_i$, $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, with $B_i$ a finite type $A$-algebra. Associatedness is a condition on the stalk and its local ring [def-trf-relative-assassin], so for any open immersion $T\subseteq Z$ one has $\operatorname{Ass}_T(G|_T)=\operatorname{Ass}_Z(G)\cap T$: both stalks and local rings at a point of $T$ are identical. Apply this to every fibre chart $(X_i)_y\subseteq X_y$. The hypothesis holds on every chart. If each chart yields a nonempty base open $V_i$, their finite intersection is nonempty since each contains the generic point of the irreducible base; on this intersection every fibre associated point is in a chart and hence in $U_y$. If $r=0$, take $V=Y$. We may work on one affine chart $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), second paragraph, finite affine covering and locality of associatedness.

proof.text: Put $N=\Gamma(X,F)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] this is a finite $B$-module, and the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] gives $F\cong\widetilde N$. On the fibre over a field $\kappa=\kappa(y)$ the coordinate ring is $B_\kappa=B\otimes_A\kappa$. The fibre module is $N_\kappa=N\otimes_A\kappa$: [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives $N\otimes_B(B\otimes_A\kappa)$, identified with $N\otimes_A\kappa$ by $n\otimes(b\otimes c)\mapsto bn\otimes c$, with inverse $n\otimes c\mapsto n\otimes(1\otimes c)$. Pullback quasi-coherence follows from [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. If $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ generate $B$ over $A$, their tensors generate $B_\kappa$ over $\kappa$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $B_\kappa$ Noetherian. Thus [lem-sfb-affine-associated-points-primes] applies to every fibre, including $K$.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), third paragraph, affine finite module and Noetherian fibre rings; Properties Tag 01PB and Divisors Tag 02OK.

proof.text: The principal opens $D(g)\subseteq U$, $g\in B$, cover $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open]. Their inverse images cover $U_K$. Since $B_K$ is Noetherian, its spectrum has the descending-chain condition on closed subsets: a descending chain of closed subsets gives an ascending chain of their radical ideals, which stabilizes. Consequently [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] gives a finite subcover of $U_K$. Choose $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in B$ with $D(g_j)\subseteq U$ and $U_K=\bigcup_jD(g_j\otimes1)$. The case $U_K=\varnothing$ allows $m=0$. Only $U_K$, rather than $U$, was required to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), third paragraph, finite principal subcover of the generic-fibre open.

proof.text: Define $\mu:N\to N^{\oplus m}$ by $n\mapsto(g_jn)_j$. Its generic-field version $\mu_K$ is injective. Indeed, let $z\in N_K$ satisfy $(g_j\otimes1)z=0$ for every $j$. Each $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_{B_K}(N_K)$ corresponds by [lem-sfb-affine-associated-points-primes] to a generic-fibre associated point, hence lies in $U_K$ and avoids some $g_j\otimes1$. That element is invertible in $(B_K)_{\mathfrak q}$, so $z/1=0$ in $(N_K)_{\mathfrak q}$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] gives $z=0$. This argument also covers an empty assassin: the cited map into the empty product is injective.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), third paragraph, injectivity of the generic multiplication map. This proves it directly using Tag 0311, without needing Tag 0565.

proof.text: Let $C=\operatorname{coker}(\mu)=N^{\oplus m}/\mu(N)$. It is a finite $B$-module: take the images of the finite generating tuples of $N^{\oplus m}$. Thus $P=N\oplus C$ is finite. Apply [lem-trf-algebra-module-simultaneous-generic-flatness] to $A\to B$ and $P$. Obtain $0\ne h\in A$ such that $P_h$ is flat as an $A$-module. The summand maps identify $P_h=N_h\oplus C_h$, so $N_h$ and $C_h$ are each $A$-flat. Explicitly, for an injection $L\to L\prime$, a vector killed after tensoring with $N_h$ maps by the split inclusion to one killed in $L\otimes_AP_h$; flatness kills that image, and the tensor of the projection sends it back to the original vector. This proves injectivity after tensoring with $N_h$, and the same inclusion/projection argument proves it for $C_h$, using the flatness definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), third paragraph, generic flatness applied simultaneously to the finite source and cokernel; Algebra Tag 051T.

proof.text: The canonical map $N_h\to N_K$ is injective. For every $0\ne a\in A$, multiplication $A\xrightarrow{a}A$ is injective because $A$ is a domain. Tensoring with the flat module $N_h$ makes multiplication by $a$ on $N_h$ injective, by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The fraction-zero criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] then says that localization at $A\setminus\{0\}$ is injective on $N_h$. This localization is $N_K$: iterated fractions identify $(n/h^r)/a$ with $n/(h^ra)$. If $z\in\ker\mu_h$, its image in $N_K$ is killed by $\mu_K$, hence is zero by Step 5, and therefore $z=0$. Thus $\mu_h$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), third paragraph, flatness implies torsion-freeness and the generic zero kernel vanishes; expanded directly from flatness and fractions, instead of quoting More on Algebra Tag 0538.

proof.text: There is a short exact sequence $0\to N_h\xrightarrow{\mu_h}N_h^{\oplus m}\to C_h\to0$. To verify the right-hand assertions directly, every fraction $c/h^r$ in $C_h$ lifts to $v/h^r$ in $(N^{\oplus m})_h$, since $N^{\oplus m}\to C$ is surjective. If $v/h^r$ maps to zero in $C_h$, the fraction-zero criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $h^e[v]=0$ in $C$ for some $e$, so $h^ev=\mu(n)$ for some $n\in N$. Then $v/h^r=\mu_h(n/h^{r+e})$. The finite direct-sum localization is coordinatewise, using a common denominator for its finitely many coordinates. This proves exactness; injectivity is Step 7.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), third paragraph, the localized short exact sequence; explicit fraction proof of its cokernel identification.

proof.text: For any $y\in D(h)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $\kappa=\kappa(y)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] with base ring $A$, short exact sequence from Step 8, flat quotient $C_h$, and module $\kappa$. It makes $\kappa\otimes_A\mu_h$ injective. Since $h$ has nonzero, hence invertible, image in $\kappa$, the map $N_h\otimes_A\kappa\to N\otimes_A\kappa$, $(n/h^r)\otimes c\mapsto n\otimes h^{-r}c$, is an isomorphism inverse to $n\otimes c\mapsto(n/1)\otimes c$. The same formula in each coordinate identifies the induced map with $\mu_\kappa:N_\kappa\to N_\kappa^{\oplus m}$, $z\mapsto((g_j\otimes1)z)_j$. Thus this precise multiplication map is injective on every fibre over $D(h)$.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), last paragraph, tensoring the short exact sequence with residue fields, using Algebra Tag 00HL.

proof.text: Fix $y\in D(h)$ and let $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_y}(F_y)$. Step 3 and [lem-sfb-affine-associated-points-primes] give a prime $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_{B_\kappa}(N_\kappa)$ corresponding to $x$. By the element-annihilator definition [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], choose $z$ with $\operatorname{Ann}(z)=\mathfrak q$. This $z$ is nonzero, since a prime ideal is proper whereas $\operatorname{Ann}(0)=B_\kappa$. If $x$ were outside every $D(g_j\otimes1)$, every $g_j\otimes1$ would belong to $\mathfrak q$, so $\mu_\kappa(z)=0$, contradicting Step 9. Hence $x\in\bigcup_jD(g_j\otimes1)\subseteq U_y$. This proves containment for the chart on the nonempty base open $D(h)$, which contains the prime $(0)$ because $h\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), last paragraph, reverse implication from injectivity to containment of associated points, written via element annihilators.

proof.text: Perform Steps 3--10 for the finitely many affine charts of Step 2. The resulting opens $D(h_i)$ all contain the generic point, so their finite intersection $V\prime$ is nonempty and open. For every $y\in V\prime$ and associated point $x\in X_y$, choose a chart containing $x$; the stalk equality of Step 2 shows it is an associated point of that fibre chart, so Step 10 puts it in $U_y$. Finally transfer $V\prime\subseteq W$ back to $Y$ as in Step 1: the homeomorphism maps it onto a nonempty open $V\subseteq V_0\subseteq Y$, and [lem-sfb-fibre-assassin-containment-base-change] identifies the two containment conditions pointwise. This gives the required $V$ with no Noetherian hypothesis on $Y$ and no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $U$.

source.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), second paragraph and conclusion, finite-chart assembly and descent from the reduced affine base.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05KP (lemma-good-case), full proof; injectivity is obtained directly from Tag 0311 rather than the two intermediate localization maps of Tag 0565.
